Guides / 01—08

Read HEX codes and RGB channels

Understand the numbers before assigning colors to text, backgrounds or controls.

Vijeron · Updated 10 October 2026

Three channels in one code

A six-digit HEX color records red, green and blue as three hexadecimal pairs. #2C5A83 means red 2C, green 5A and blue 83; each pair corresponds to a value from 0 to 255. Three-digit notation such as #ABC doubles each digit to #AABBCC.

Separate the code from its appearance

The same code may look different across displays, brightness settings, lighting and surrounding colors. For interface decisions, record the exact code and inspect a sample at the actual text size and background.

Record color roles

Do not label a color only blue or green. Record its job, such as main text, surface, border or focus. Roles make later palette changes easier to review.

Reproducible example

#2C5A83 equals RGB (44, 90, 131). The first hexadecimal pair, 2C, equals decimal 44.

What to check

Two colors that differ on large swatches may still be hard to distinguish as small text.
